newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 7.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - The central bank is prepared to defend the stability of the crown, according to a member of its banking council, Miroslav Hrncir. Another council member, Ludek Niedermayer said yesterday that a possible solution would be to increase interest rates.

- Members of the cabinet decided yesterday that the government budget for next year will be planned with a slight surplus. Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik proposes that the 1998 budget increase nominally by seven percent.
- The cabinet should decide today on changes to the law for businesses which do not pay social-security insurance.
- Skoda Plzen should sell a licence for making small and medium sized turbine steamboats to Hyundai.
- Shareholders of Poldi Steel dismissed Vladimir and Marko Stehlik from their places in the supervisory council and the board of directors yesterday.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - If the Czech economy were to be put in the hands of the opposition Social Democrats, one of the party's first actions to save the domestic market would be to introduce import charges of 10 to 20 percent on consumer goods. The chairman of the party, Milos Zeman, wants to present his party's "package" at the next parliament meeting.

- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said yesterday that the capital market quickly got through its first phase of development and now requires a more standard form, which the cabinet's measures should give it.

- If privatisation of Investicni a Postovni Banka (IPB) is prolonged, it could negatively affect plans for Agrobanka's preservation. The timed plan for both privatisations allows potential investors who lose in the tender for IPB to enter the tender for Agrobanka.

- Trinecke Zelezarny obtained a government order for Turkish railways worth 600 million crowns through its general business partner and majority owner Moravia Steel. It should supply 40,000 tonnes of rails to Turkey by the end of the year.

PRAVO - The European Commission of the EU expects that the Czech Republic will formally react to the EU's unfavourable attitude concerning the imposition of import deposit requirements by May 12. The commission will react to this answer and not to the comments of leaders of the Czech cabinet.
- The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) estimates that not even next year's GDP will be on the same level as GDP in 1989.
- Cimex Holding wants to participate in the public tender for the privatisation of 52.46 procent of Zelezarny Chomutov.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The director of AB Barrandov, Vaclav Marhoul, was dismissed from his function yesterday by the board of directors at the company. The majority owner, Moravia Steel, put Pavel Prerovsky in his place.
- The chairman of the Christian Democrats, Josef Lux should announce the name of the new Regional Development Minister at today's cabinet meeting.

- Ministers decided on building a state information system yesterday. The Labour, Interior and Finance Ministers will prepare material for the system's priorities and how its construction will be approached by the end of June.

- The Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting warned operators of Nova Television for the second time of the possibility of its licence being taken away due to conduct of its director, Vladimir Zelezny, on the programme Call the Director.
- The modernised tank T-72 CZ from Vojensky Opravarensky Podnik had its world debut yesterday on the first day of the international munitions trade fair IDET 1997.

- After meeting with Slovak Agriculture Minister Peter Baco, Czech Agriculture Minister Josef Lux announced that Slovakia is not preparing import quotas for any agricultural commodities other than alcohol.
